seo.metaTitle: Galt Workplace Injury Claims | Free Case Review
seo.metaDescription: Hurt on the job in Galt, CA? Get a free case review from an attorney who handles workers' comp and third-party workplace injury claims.

hero.subtitle: If you were injured working near SR-99 or one of Galt's warehouses and distribution yards, we can help you understand your legal options at no cost. We handle Sacramento County workplace injury cases involving workers' compensation and third-party claims.

about.title: Galt Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Galt's economy leans on agriculture, trucking, and logistics operations spread along SR-99 and the industrial stretches near Twin Cities Road, which means workplace injuries here often involve forklifts, delivery vehicles, farm equipment, or falls on loading docks. California generally requires injured workers to go through workers' compensation rather than suing their employer directly, but that's not always the end of the story. When a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another company's driver contributed to your injury, you may have a separate claim outside the workers' comp system. We don't practice workers' compensation exclusively — we handle workplace injury claims that may involve multiple legal paths. There's no cost to discuss your case, and no obligation to move forward. A quick conversation can clarify whether your situation involves more than just a workers' comp filing.
commonInjuries: Falls from loading docks or ladders

items.title: We Help You See Past the Workers' Comp Wall
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against an employer, but a negligent third party like a subcontractor or equipment maker can open a separate claim. We can evaluate whether that applies to you.

items.title: Timing Matters and We Help You Move Fast
items.desc: You generally have 30 days to report a workplace injury to your employer, and any third-party claim carries a 2-year deadline. Getting started early helps protect both timelines.

items.title: Retaliation Protection Guidance
items.desc: California law prohibits employer retaliation for reporting a workplace injury. Our team can help you understand your rights if you feel pressured after filing.

items.question: I was hurt driving a delivery route through Galt for my employer — is that just a workers' comp case?
items.answer: Not necessarily. If another driver, perhaps on SR-99 or Twin Cities Road, caused the collision, that driver's negligence could support a separate third-party claim alongside your workers' comp benefits. We can review the details and let you know which claims apply.

items.question: What happens if my employer doesn't want me to report the injury?
items.answer: California law makes it illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting a workplace injury, and you generally have 30 days to make that report. If you're facing pushback, our team can advise you on next steps.

items.question: Is there any cost to discuss my case with your team?
items.answer: No, there is no cost to review your situation. We typically work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost or obligation to move forward.
